tickets.title: Table Partitioning by Date Range
tickets.description: Creates a partitioned table for orders using date ranges to split orders by calendar years.
tasks: Creates a partitioned table for orders using date ranges to split orders by calendar years.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and querying.
tickets.evaluation: `check_table_partitioned("partitioned_orders")` `verify_partition_boundaries("partitioned_orders")` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts if partition boundaries are set correctly. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for using multi-column range partition boundaries. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for defining MAXVALUE fallback tables.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without backticks.
hints: Review the MySQL documentation for exact syntax.
Test your queries in smaller chunks first.

solution.query.sql:
CREATE TABLE partitioned_orders (
      id INT,
      customer_id INT,
      total_amount NUMERIC(10,2),
      created_at DATE,
      PRIMARY KEY (id, created_at)
    )
    PARTITION BY RANGE COLUMNS(created_at) (
      PARTITION p2023 VALUES LESS THAN ('2024-01-01'),
      PARTITION p2024 VALUES LESS THAN ('2025-01-01'),
      PARTITION pmax VALUES LESS THAN (MAXVALUE)
    );

tickets.title: Reporting View Enforcements
tickets.description: Defines a reporting view with the CHECK OPTION constraint to extract customer summaries safely.
tasks: Defines a reporting view with the CHECK OPTION constraint to extract customer summaries safely.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and querying.
tickets.evaluation: `check_view_exists("customer_financial_summary")` `verify_check_option_enforced()` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts if view aggregates correctly. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts if nested joins resolve efficiently. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for using `WITH CHECK OPTION` write bounds.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without backticks.
hints: Remember to use GROUP BY for aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVG.

solution.query.sql:
CREATE VIEW customer_financial_summary AS
    SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS lifetime_value
    FROM customers c
    JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
    WHERE c.status = 'active'
    GROUP BY c.id
    WITH CHECK OPTION;
